title: Capacity Control Panel — wireframe notes & grooming
content:
Purpose:
Quick capture of ideas and grooming notes for the Dedicated Capacity "Capacity Control Panel" (admin-facing console). Focus: GPU pool management, autoscaling rules, burst capacity, and reservation timeline UX. 

Status summary (where we are):
- High-level concept vetted in product sync 2025-11-07.
- PM asked for two flows: 1) operator-first (bulk editing / quick actions) and 2) team-facing (reservation bookings + cost preview).
- Engineering flagged constraints: backend exposes pool / slot APIs but reservation conflict detection is eventual — need UX to show provisional/conflict states.

Primary goals for this panel (user stories):
- As a cluster admin, I want a single view of all GPU pools with health and capacity so I can decide where to route traffic.
- As a platform engineer, I want to preview cost and latency impact of enabling bursts so I can approve/deny changes quickly.
- As a product owner, I want to reserve capacity windows for customer X and see conflicts with upcoming rollouts.

Personas considered:
- Platform Admin (can edit pools, create reservations, override autoscale): needs bulk operations and audit trail.
- Team Lead/Engineer (can request reservations, view reserved windows): needs clear request status and cost estimate.
- SRE (read metrics + incidents): needs fast access to metrics and ability to pin fallbacks.

Wireframe areas / sketches (rough, text layout):
1) Top nav: [Left] Redwood logo | [Center] "Capacity Control Panel" title + quick filter chips (region, tier, model tag) | [Right] "Create Reservation" + user menu

2) Fleet table (primary canvas) columns: Pool name | Region | HW type | Slots used / total (graph) | Autoscale policy (label) | Burst bucket (label) | Cost/hr estimate | Conflicts (badge) | Actions (ellipsis)
- Row interactions: hover -> quick actions preview (scale up, open reservation modal, open metrics). Clicking pool -> pool detail flyout.

3) Pool detail flyout (right side):
- Header: pool name, edit button, last updated timestamp, owner/team tag
- Mini metrics: 1m/5m tail latency, avg token/sec, error rate, current queued requests
- Autoscale panel: current policy summary (min/max/scale-step), visual timeline of recent scaling events (stacked area)
- Burst panel: available burst credits, last burst usage, estimated cost of 1-hour burst at p95 load
- Reservation timeline: calendar strip showing reserved windows (clickable)

4) Reservation modal (create/request flow):
- Steps: Requestor fills start/end, min slots, max slots (optional), justification, linked PR/ticket, cost preview toggle, required approvals (list).
- UI behavior: if conflict with existing reservation -> modal shows conflict rows with suggested adjustments. "Provisional" state shown if backend not yet confirmed.
- Acceptance UX: requestor can choose auto-suggested fallback pools (based on model tag and region).

5) Autoscale policy editor (inline / small modal):
- Presets: conservative | balanced | aggressive | custom
- Custom: min, target-utilization (%), max, cooldown seconds, scale-step, prefer-newer-instances toggle (affects placement).
- Simulation mode: preview effect on historic traffic (1h/6h/24h) with tokenized cost delta and latency percentile delta. Gray/green/red heatmap.

6) Quick actions toolbar (top of table):
- Bulk select pools -> batch update autoscale policy / add/remove burst credits / open reservations in bulk / export CSV.

7) Cost and SLA preview bar (bottom sticky):
- Live estimate for current table filters: projected hourly cost, projected 99th pct latency (based on model profiles), risk indicators. "Apply changes" confirms performed operations.

UX details / micro-copy notes (things to be careful about):
- Use "provisional" vs "confirmed" for reservations — avoid ambiguous words like "pending" alone.
- For burst credits show both "credits remaining" and "estimated dollars if used" because teams think in dollars.
- Conflict messaging: surface what wins (e.g., "Reservation A has higher priority; your request will be queued") and provide one-click negotiation suggestions.
- Autoscale simulation must be conservative: show confidence band and not promise exact latency.

Accessibility notes:
- Timeline must be keyboard-navigable; reservations should have high-contrast borders and aria labels for start/end times.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Priority model for conflicting reservations: do we consider "team tier" + "request timestamp" + "override flag"? Need policy doc. (Action: Samir to propose priority rules, JIRA-INF-1024)
- Burst accounting: are credits per-pool, per-org, or pooled across pools in a region? Backend has partial support for pooled credits but API lacks attribution. (Action: infra team to clarify by 2025-12-01)
- Reservation provisionality: currently backend creates a provisional reservation id then runs distributed lock; UX must surface eventual consistency windows (seconds -> minutes). How to show "locking" state in timeline?

Backlog / grooming items (prioritized):
- P0: Reservation create/edit flow + conflict resolution modal (3w dev, 1w UX polish) -> JIRA-INF-1024
- P0: Fleet table with bulk actions and quick filter by region/model (2w dev) -> split: backend API gating (1w) + frontend (1w)
- P1: Autoscale policy editor + simulation mode (2w dev + 1w infra metrics hooks) -> add feature flag
- P1: Burst credits UI (show credits and cost preview) + allocation endpoint (2w)
- P2: Audit trail view within pool detail (1w)
- P3: CSV export / scheduling templates (sprint stretch)

Acceptance criteria (for first shipment - MVP):
- Create reservation: user can submit a reservation request, see provisional state, and see the reservation appear on the timeline within 30s of submit (unless conflict).
- Pool table: shows live slots used/total with <= 30s staleness and supports filters by region and hw type.
- Quick action bulk edits: update autoscale policy for selected pools and reflect changes in UI within 60s.
- Autoscale editor baseline: support preset policies and show simulation results for last 1h of traffic (using historical metrics backfill).

Design constraints / backend notes (for eng):
- API endpoints available: GET /pools, POST /reservations (creates provisional entry), GET /reservations, POST /pools/{id}/autoscale
- Missing/needs: endpoint to simulate autoscale (suggested: POST /simulations/autoscale), burst attribution endpoint
- UX should tolerate eventual consistency: avoid locking the whole UI while server-side locks are resolving

Edge cases to test / QA checklist:
- Overlapping reservations with different priorities -> ensure top-priority wins and lower shows "rescheduled" state
- Autoscale min > current slots -> instant allocation path (verify billing spike displayed)
- Burst usage exhaustion mid-flight -> fallback policy triggers (verify rollback UX and alerting)

Notes to designers (quick):
- Low-fidelity frames: 6 screens (fleet table, pool detail flyout, reservation modal, autoscale editor, bulk action modal, cost preview strip)
- Make color system consistent with alerts: orange for provisional/needs-attention, red for conflicts, green for confirmed/healthy
- Use sparklines for quick metrics, reserve larger chart space in flyout for detailed tracing

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Elena: iterate on low-fi prototypes and upload to Figma (due 2025-12-05)
- Samir: draft reservation priority rules and post to Confluence (due 2025-11-22)
- Asha: confirm burst accounting model with infra and update linked artifacts (due 2025-11-30)
- Marcus: prototype API for autoscale simulation and open a PR (link above)

Quick links / references (working):
- Existing pool API spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pools-api (draft)
- Design tokens and component library: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system
- Slack discussion: #capacity-panel (thread t/ops-ux-reservations)

Random brainstorm fragments (keep for context):
- "simulate future: predict starvation windows and auto-suggest reservations to patch"
- "allow cross-team swap: two teams commit to swap windows -> negotiator modal"
- "reservation templates for daily/weekly recurrences"

Notes to self:
- Capture screenshots of current prod reservation timeline (Riley) before next design review.
- Don't overpromise real-time guarantees in first release.

-- end of doc --
